clue.text: Be stumped by an eviction order!

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batsman who is stumped is dismissed, i.e. loses their wicket
a curt command telling someone to leave the premises

explanation.surface: A cricketer dismissed by the wicketkeeper compared with a tenant being thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: Being stumped is one of the ways a cricket batsman is dismissed; the exclamation is the shouted command to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of the phrase: a batsman's dismissal in cricket, and the brusque instruction to leave a place.

clue.text: Leaving home and getting high

definitions.meaning: departing, setting out
of food, becoming smelly and starting to rot

explanation.surface: Moving out and taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' here is the smell of meat or game turning bad, not intoxication.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means departing, and also of food spoiling or turning rancid.

clue.text: Boastful and stilted conversation

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective, the answer a noun phrase for bragging speech; used attributively it describes boastful words

parts.note: someone on stilts is raised up high, so stilted gives a word for lofty
conversation is a synonym for talk, speech

explanation.surface: Pompous, stiff chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stilted' looks like formal or stiff but is read as being on stilts, hence lofty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means exaggerated, bragging speech, the kind a boastful person indulges in.

clue.text: Middle of awful nasty bone in the arm

indicators.note: Middle of says the answer is in the interior of the following words, a run of letters across them

explanation.surface: A nasty fracture in the forearm.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the two long bones of the forearm, on the little-finger side.

clue.text: Certainly no bent policeman could make legitimate arrest

definitions.meaning: an honest officer, the opposite of a corrupt one, read literally as a just constable
the idiom a criminal uses conceding that he was caught fairly

explanation.surface: An honest officer, not a corrupt one, is the kind who makes a proper arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' is British slang for corrupt. The idiom is the old-fashioned phrase a caught crook says, admitting the arrest is justified.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase names an honest constable; as an idiom it is a criminal's admission that he was caught justly.

clue.text: Comrade who gives (or maybe requires) timely help

definitions.text: Comrade who gives (or maybe requires) timely help

parts.words: Comrade who gives (or maybe requires) timely help
parts.note: the proverb says a pal who helps when you are in difficulty is a true one, but the phrase could equally describe a pal who himself needs help

explanation.surface: A true pal supports you when it matters, or perhaps needs support.
explanation.walkthrough: From the proverb about a true companion helping in hard times; the bracket notes the phrase's other reading, a companion who is himself in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial phrase describes a true companion who helps when one is in difficulty.

clue.text: Earliest centre for missionaries

indicators.note: centre for says the answer is the run of letters at the very heart of the following word

explanation.surface: The first base for spreading the gospel.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters at the exact centre of 'missionaries' name the Scottish island where St Columba founded his abbey in 563, the base for converting the Picts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inner Hebridean island was the base of St Columba's mission, an early cradle of Christianity in Scotland.

clue.text: Hot pepper I needed after feverish cold

indicators.note: needed after says the I is placed behind the cold word in the answer

parts.note: a chill is a cold with shivering and fever

explanation.surface: Someone with a feverish cold craves a hot pepper to warm up.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hot-tasting capsicum pod, a spicy pepper.

clue.text: Polite request to make others happy

definitions.meaning: the courteous word added when asking for something
to give pleasure or satisfaction to people

explanation.surface: Asking nicely to keep people content.
explanation.definitionFit: The courteous word used when asking, and a verb meaning give satisfaction or delight.

clue.text: Where property developers invest but not on the coast

definitions.meaning: developers put their money into ground and plots, read as two words
away from the sea, in the interior of a country

explanation.surface: Developers sink their money into sites away from the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer says what developers put money into; as one word it means away from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrase, developers buy plots of ground; as one word it means located in the interior, far from the shore.

clue.text: VIP racket

definitions.meaning: a very important person, a bigwig
a loud din, a lot of sound

explanation.surface: A celebrity is making a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigwig is an idiomatic synonym for a VIP, and literally a loud din is a racket.

clue.text: Reprimand for not getting togged up

definitions.meaning: a severe telling-off
wearing casual clothes rather than smart ones

explanation.surface: Being scolded for failing to dress smartly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Togged up' is British for dressed smartly; the answer read literally means dressing casually.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe scolding, and literally the act of choosing casual over formal clothes.

clue.text: Georgia confronts one who abstains from world trade agreement

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
TT, teetotal, describes someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A country takes on a refusenik over a global commerce deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confronts' is a link here: GA stands before TT. The answer is the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, the forerunner of the World Trade Organization.
explanation.definitionFit: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade was the postwar international treaty governing commerce between nations.

clue.text: Old hag found by King Charles!

definitions.text: Old hag found by King Charles!

parts.words: Old hag found by King Charles!
parts.note: King Charles the First signed as Carolus Rex, and CR with the numeral one spelt out yields a word for a withered old woman

explanation.surface: A monarch comes upon a witch.
explanation.walkthrough: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles; adding ONE (Charles the First) gives the word. The clue leaves the ONE to be inferred, hence the exclamation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a standard term for an ugly, withered old woman, a synonym of hag.

clue.text: Part of Palm Sunday's charity collection

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A church collection is taken on the Sunday before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or goods given to the poor are donations, traditionally collected in church.

clue.text: Certain to be on the way

definitions.meaning: sure, destined to happen
heading for a destination

explanation.surface: Sure to be travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: It means destined or sure, and also heading towards somewhere, as a train headed for a city.

clue.text: Excavated with concealed explosives

definitions.meaning: dug out from the ground, as coal or ore
laid with buried bombs, as a minefield

explanation.surface: Dug up and booby-trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Dug out as ore from a pit, and also laid with hidden bombs, as a field or harbour.

clue.text: Eager to be drunk on gin or whisky

definitions.meaning: keen and lively, full of energy
spirits are strong distilled drinks such as gin or whisky, so someone tipsy on them is literally filled with them

explanation.surface: Someone keen to get tipsy on hard liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means lively and keen; taken literally it describes a person filled with distilled liquor.

clue.text: Spill the beans, so don't sell them

definitions.meaning: to reveal a secret
hand items over free of charge

explanation.surface: Reveal the secret, then donate the beans rather than sell them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spill the beans' is an idiom for revealing a secret; the second part plays on literal beans being handed out free.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means betray a secret, and also donate something free rather than charge for it.

clue.text: Partner and I order an amphibious pet

indicators.note: order as a verb means arrange, so these letters are put into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple buy a pet for the pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater turtle that lives both on land and in water, often kept by children.

clue.text: EEC remaining committed to the old French political system

indicators.note: committed suggests being sent off and changed, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The European Economic Community stays loyal to France's pre-revolutionary regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Committed' is the anagram signal on EEC plus REMAINING. The answer is the regime of France before the 1789 Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means former government, the absolute monarchy swept away by the Revolution.

clue.text: Bivouac on American university grounds

parts.note: a bivouac is a temporary encampment
US abbreviates United States, so American

explanation.surface: Students pitch tents on an American college site.
explanation.definitionFit: The grounds and buildings of a college or university.

clue.text: Jack gets accustomed to being sworn at

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman
used to something is accustomed to it

explanation.surface: A sailor grows hardened to being cursed.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack, from jack tar, is a sailor; AB is an able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulted verbally, subjected to swearing and invective.

clue.text: A fall in the ocean upset the brothers' father

indicators.note: upset in a down clue would mean turned over; here it says the word for a falling tide is read backwards

parts.note: an ebb is the falling of the tide in the sea

explanation.surface: A drop in the sea level overturned the monks' superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns EBB round to BBE, which follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title for an abbot or priest, i.e. the head of a community of monks.

clue.text: One who encourages a moth?

definitions.meaning: a person who urges others on, who eggs them on
a species of moth, such as the oak variety, is so named

explanation.surface: A cheerleader is likened to a moth.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a person who goads others on; also the name of a family of large brownish moths.

clue.text: Breed back

definitions.meaning: to raise or bring up animals or children
the hind part, the posterior

explanation.surface: A breed returns.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to raise young; as a noun it means the hindmost part.

clue.text: Indicative of future resolution

definitions.meaning: the auxiliary verb used to form the future tense
determination, firmness of purpose

explanation.surface: A sign of what is to come is a firm resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: The auxiliary forming the future tense in grammar, and a noun meaning determination or volition.

clue.text: Daily help in the orchard

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the word that follows, as a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A cleaner working among the fruit trees.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' in Britain is a cleaning woman who comes in each day, also called a charwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a cleaning lady, short for charwoman.

clue.text: Father's to be a member of a committee to relay information

parts.note: PA is an informal word for dad, with the possessive s

parts.words: to be a member of a committee
parts.note: to sit on a board or panel is to serve as a member

explanation.surface: Dad will join a panel in order to spread news.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to hand something along, such as a message, to the next person.

clue.text: Attend if put to shame

definitions.meaning: to turn up, to be present
to embarrass by outdoing or exposing someone

explanation.surface: Turn up if humiliated.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means arrive or be present, and also embarrass someone by outperforming them.

clue.text: Second job profile

definitions.meaning: work done in addition to one's main occupation
an outline seen from the side

explanation.surface: Someone's second occupation features in their profile.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary occupation pursued alongside a main one; also, literally, a side outline.

clue.text: Colour marker about to be used with artificial fabric

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
rayon is a synthetic textile made from cellulose

explanation.surface: A dye marking is about to be applied to a synthetic cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick of coloured wax or chalk used for drawing, a coloured marker.
